epidemiology: Most common ovarian germ cell tumor, accounting for 20-25% of all ovarian neoplasms. Peak incidence in women aged 20-40 years.
pathophysiology: Arises from totipotent germ cells containing tissues from ectoderm (skin, sebaceous glands, hair), mesoderm (bone, fat, cartilage), and endoderm (thyroid, gastrointestinal).

classic_ultrasound_triad.feature_1: Dermoid Plug (Rokitansky Nodule): Intracystic hyperechoic mural nodule with posterior acoustic shadowing.
classic_ultrasound_triad.feature_2: Dermoid Mesh / Dots and Lines: Echogenic floating lines and dots caused by hair fibers within liquid sebaceous fluid.
classic_ultrasound_triad.feature_3: Tip-of-the-Iceberg Sign: Highly echogenic anterior mass margin with complete posterior acoustic shadowing obscuring deep structures.
classic_ultrasound_triad.feature_4: Fat-Fluid Level: Dependent layering of lipid fluid over denser aqueous or cellular content.

doppler_characteristics: Avascular internal contents (Color Score 1). Rokitansky nodule may show subtle peripheral rim flow, but internal vascularity is absent in typical benign dermoids.
orads_category: O-RADS 2 (Almost Certainly Benign, Risk < 1% if classic features present and < 10 cm).
iota_rules_alignment: Satisfies IOTA B-Rule B3 (Presence of acoustic shadows).
differential_diagnosis: Hemorrhagic corpus luteum (distinguished by absence of acoustic shadowing, presence of peripheral ring-of-fire vascularity, and resolution on follow-up).
Endometrioma (homogeneous ground-glass echoes, lacks dense acoustic shadowing).
Immature teratoma (malignant, contains prominent vascularized solid components without shadowing).
management: Asymptomatic classic dermoid < 5 cm in premenopausal women can be observed with annual ultrasound. Masses > 5 cm or symptomatic cysts are managed with laparoscopic cystectomy to prevent ovarian torsion.
